lead: Breech is a longitudinal lie with the buttocks or feet presenting and the head in the fundus; the denominator is the sacrum. It is the commonest malpresentation: 25% before 28 wk but 3–4% at term. The danger is the aftercoming head.
f: Lie: long axis (longitudinal, transverse, oblique) · Presentation: lowest part · Attitude: flexion or extension · Denominator: occiput, sacrum, mentum, acromion · Malpresentation: not vertex (breech, face, brow, shoulder) · Malposition: vertex with the occiput not anterior (OT, OP)

tr: OP is a malposition, not a malpresentation

f: Frank 65% (hips flexed, knees extended; commonest in primigravidae) · Complete 25% (hips and knees flexed) · Footling 10% (highest cord prolapse risk) · Causes: idiopathic; prematurity (commonest association); uterine anomaly, fibroid; poly- or oligohydramnios; praevia, cornual placenta; twins, hydrocephalus, anencephaly; contracted pelvis; lax multiparous uterus

sc: Breech in 3 pregnancies in a row → Uterine anomaly

f: Discomfort under the ribs; kicks felt low · Hard ballotable head in the fundus; FHS at or above the umbilicus · VE: ischial tuberosities and anus in one line, sacrum, genitalia, feet, meconium on the glove · Ultrasound: type, EFW, head flexion, placenta, liquor, anomalies (2–3 times more common) · About 30% found only in labour · Face vs breech: face has gums and a triangle of mouth and malar bones

sc: Thick meconium in a breech in the second stage → Often normal (compressed bowel)

f: Fetal: cord prolapse (footling 15%, complete 5%, frank 0.5%), trapped aftercoming head, intracranial bleed, fractures, Erb palsy, liver and adrenal tears, higher perinatal death · Maternal: CS risks, tears, PPH, a scar for next time

tr: The body can slip through a cervix that is not fully dilated (preterm, footling); the bigger head is then trapped

f: Offer at 36 wk primigravida, 37 wk multipara · Labour ward with theatre; scan, CTG, terbutaline 0.25 mg SC · Forward roll, no force · After: CTG 30 min; anti-D 500 IU + Kleihauer if RhD-negative · Success about 50% (40% primi, 60% multi) · Contraindicated: praevia, APH, twins, CS needed anyway, ruptured membranes, severe oligohydramnios, fetal compromise · Complications: transient FHR slowing, abruption, cord accident, feto-maternal bleed · Knee-chest position does not work

sc: Primigravida, breech at 37 wk, normal liquor → ECV
Bleeding and FHR 80 after ECV → Abruption: emergency CS

f: Assisted vaginal breech: frank or complete, EFW 2.0–3.8 kg (RCOG; local units often 2.5 kg), flexed head, no FGR or other problem, adequate pelvis, skilled staff · Elective CS at 39 wk: footling, EFW over 3.8 or under 2.0 kg, star-gazing head, other CS indication, her choice, first twin breech · Perinatal death about 0.5 per 1000 with planned CS vs 2 per 1000 with planned vaginal breech (RCOG) · In labour: criteria not met or early labour → CS · Preterm breech: CS often chosen; steroids, MgSO₄

sc: Breech with a star-gazing head on scan → Caesarean

f: Continuous CTG, paediatrician, no early ARM; slow progress = CS, not oxytocin · Hands off: push from above, never pull from below · Umbilicus to head in about 4 min; head delivered slowly · Pinard for extended legs · Løvset for extended arms · Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit for the head (first choice) · Piper forceps when MSV fails · Breech extraction only for the second twin or acute distress at full dilatation · After: check clavicle, humerus, femur, Erb palsy; hip check for DDH

sc: Arms extended above the head → Løvset manoeuvre
Arm cannot move after a breech birth → Erb palsy or fractured humerus/clavicle
